The statute described outlines the core requirements for valid consent under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Legally, this means that consent cannot be assumed through silence, pre-ticked boxes, or inactivity. Instead, it must be an active, affirmative action that is specific to the data processing activity, informed by clear information about what is being collected, and given freely without coercion. For businesses, this imposes a strict compliance burden to demonstrate that they have obtained such consent before processing personal data. For individuals, it establishes a robust right to control their personal information, ensuring they are aware of and agree to how their data is used. Failure to meet these standards can result in significant regulatory penalties and legal liability for the data controller.
